newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London track Wall Street gains.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London track Wall Street gains.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks in London were led higher on Monday, helped by continued strength on Wall Street and solid gains in HSBC Holdings, dealers said.
Trading volume remained thin, however, as the Hong Kong bourse remained shut for a public holiday.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index surged 215 points higher to 1,4870.76 by 1432 GMT. In Hong Kong on Friday the Hang Seng was up 140 points to 14,655.13.

"We have just been pushing ahead to try an equate for Friday's move on Wall Street," said one dealer. "There has been a general mark-up but most of the business has been in the banks and Hong Kong Telecom."
HSBC Holdings led the gainers, shadowing bouyant UK bank shares. The stock was up HK$6.75 at HK$234.75 compared with a close of HK$228 in Hong Kong.

The Dow Industrials Average as up around 50 points in early U.S. trade after chalking up a record close on Friday which was providing an extra boost for shares, but dealers said key U.S. economic data later this week could limit potential gains.
"The (Hong Kong) market could possibly push up to the 15,000 trading range," one said. "But people may want to sit on their hands until the figures are out of the way."
